title: Establishing credibility of implicit finite element models for hip resurfacing load transfer and stress shielding: a two-model, two-mechanism V&V40 study
device: Cemented femoral hip resurfacing component (Co–Cr cap with PMMA mantle and short peg)

models.name: Model H: Homogeneous bonded-interface femur
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static FEA of a resurfaced femur with linear-elastic, homogeneous bone; fully bonded cement–bone and cap–cement interfaces; computes cortical/cancellous strain fields, strain energy density maps, interface tractions, and load share indices under activity-specific joint and muscle forces.

models.name: Model P: Patient-specific heterogeneous, cohesive-interface femur
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static FEA with CT-mapped heterogeneous, orthotropic bone properties; cohesive contact at cement–bone interface, frictional contact at cap–cement; computes spatial load transfer, tensile strain bands at the femoral neck, cement mantle stresses, and remodeling stimuli under multi-load cases.

mechanisms.name: M1: Proximal stress shielding during level walking
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Chronic reduction in proximal femoral mechanical stimulus can drive bone resorption and loss of support for the resurfacing component.

mechanisms.name: M2: Femoral neck tensile strain concentration under varus placement during stair descent
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Elevated tensile strains at the superior femoral neck are associated with increased risk of early neck fracture after resurfacing.

deviation.detail: All credibility factor ratings are reported on a 0–5 Credibility Level Index (CLI) for each model×mechanism pairing, with acceptance defined as CLI ≥ 3.5.
